question_text: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for evaluation of easy bruising. He has met all developmental milestones. Vital signs are within normal limits. He is at the 50th percentile for height and weight. Physical examination shows velvety, fragile skin that can be stretched further than normal and multiple ecchymoses. Joint range of motion is increased. A defect in which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

                    ### Question
                    A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for evaluation of easy bruising. He has met all developmental milestones. Vital signs are within normal limits. He is at the 50th percentile for height and weight. Physical examination shows velvety, fragile skin that can be stretched further than normal and multiple ecchymoses. Joint range of motion is increased. A defect in which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. α-collagen triple helix formation
opb. α1-antitrypsin production
opc. Fibrillin-1 glycoprotein production
opd. Proline and lysine hydroxylation
ope. Lysine-hydroxylysine cross-linking

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of easy bruising, fragile skin, increased joint range of motion, and multiple ecchymoses in this 5-year-old boy is highly suggestive of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS), a connective tissue disorder. The underlying defect in EDS is primarily related to collagen synthesis, particularly the formation of the collagen triple helix, which is crucial for the structural integrity of connective tissues. The reasoning chains consistently point to a defect in α-collagen triple helix formation as the most likely cause of this patient's condition, supported by the evidence that connects bruising and fragile skin to connective tissue diseases like EDS. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's condition is a defect in α-collagen triple helix formation.
